listening.script: Welcome to Central City! My name is Sarah and I have lived in this wonderful city for five years. Today, I want to share some useful information for visitors. Central City is famous for its large green park, which is open every day from seven in the morning until nine at night. If you like shopping, the main shopping street is Market Street. It has many traditional shops and modern cafes. Transport in the city is very convenient. You can take the red bus, which costs only two dollars per trip. The underground train is faster, but it is currently closed for repairs until next month. If you need assistance during your stay, the tourist information center is located opposite the central library. They can give you free maps and advice about local events. I hope you enjoy your time exploring our beautiful city and discover everything it has to offer!

items.q: What will take place in the outdoor courtyard at five in the evening?

listening.script: Welcome everyone to the annual International Cultural Exhibition. This year, our focus is on traditional textile arts from around the world. On the ground floor, you will find an extraordinary collection of hand-woven silk scarves from Central Asia, showcasing vibrant patterns that have been preserved for centuries. As you move upstairs to the main gallery, don't miss the exhibition dedicated to Indigenous Australian dot painting, where local artists will be holding interactive workshops every afternoon at two o'clock. Registration for these workshops is free, but places are limited to fifteen participants per session to ensure a hands-on experience. Finally, the outdoor courtyard will feature live folk music performances starting at five in the evening, alongside food stalls serving authentic regional dishes. Please remember that taking photographs with flash is strictly prohibited inside the museum galleries, although regular photography is allowed in the courtyard area. We hope you enjoy your visit today!

listening.title: Chuqur dengiz mikroorganizmlarining ilmiy tadqiqoti

items.q: What primary energy source was used by the newly discovered sub-population of microorganisms?
items.exp: Matnga ko'ra, oltingugurt birikmalariga tayanadi degan taxminlarga qaramay, olimlar vodorod gazidan asosiy energiya manbai sifatida foydalanuvchi kichik guruhni kashf etishdi.

items.q: What enables the proteins of these extremophiles to remain stable at high temperatures?
items.exp: Oqsillar odatiy vodorod bog'lanishlari o'rniga zich ionli bog'lanishlar tarmog'iga ega bo'lganligi sababli yuqori haroratda o'z tuzilishini saqlaydi.

items.q: Which astronomical locations are suggested as possible habitats for similar life forms?
items.exp: Matnda Yevropa va Enselad kabi muzli yo'ldoshlarning okean osti qatlamlarida shunga o'xshash hayot shakllari bo'lishi mumkinligi ta'kidlangan.

items.q: Where will the research team's findings be released next month?
opts: In the International Marine Biology Review
In the Journal of Oceanographic Sciences
items.exp: Ekspeditsiya topilmalari kelasi oyda 'Journal of Oceanographic Sciences' jurnalida chop etiladi.

listening.script: Recent deep-sea expeditions near the Mariana Trench have uncovered surprising metabolic adaptations in marine microorganisms living near hydrothermal vents. Contrary to previous assumptions that these organisms relied strictly on chemosynthesis driven by sulfur compounds, researchers discovered a sub-population that utilizes hydrogen gas as their primary energy source. This metabolic flexibility allows them to survive sudden fluctuations in mineral output from the vents. Furthermore, structural analysis of their cellular membranes revealed novel heat-resistant proteins capable of functioning at temperatures exceeding one hundred and twenty degrees Celsius. These proteins maintain structural integrity due to dense networks of ionic bonds rather than standard hydrogen bonds. Marine biologists hypothesize that these extremophiles could offer vital insights into potential extraterrestrial life forms, particularly those that might inhabit sub-surface oceans on icy moons such as Europa or Enceladus. The expedition's findings will be published in next month's edition of the Journal of Oceanographic Sciences.

listening.script: Welcome to the City Central Market. My name is Sarah, and today I will show you our famous local food section. On your left, you can find fresh bread made every morning by our local bakers. The bakery opens early at six o'clock, so the bread is always warm and fresh. Next to the bakery, there is a large fruit stall. They sell sweet red apples, bananas, and juicy oranges from local farms. The oranges are very cheap today, only two dollars for a kilogram. If you walk straight ahead, you will see the seafood counter. They sell fresh fish caught from the nearby lake this morning. Finally, near the exit, we have a small café. Many people like to stop there to drink vegetable soup and tea. The café is famous for its delicious homemade cakes, which cost three dollars each. Please enjoy your time exploring our market today!

listening.script: Welcome to the City Sports Complex. We are thrilled to announce our newly renovated facilities, which will officially open to the public this Thursday. Members can now enjoy an upgraded indoor swimming pool, which has been heated to twenty-eight degrees Celsius for comfort. Additionally, we have expanded our gymnasium by adding twenty new cardio machines and a dedicated area for functional fitness training. Please note that our opening hours have changed. We will now open at six in the morning and close at ten in the evening from Monday to Saturday, while Sunday hours remain nine to five. Standard membership fees will increase by five percent next month, but existing members can lock in their current rates by renewing before Friday. Finally, all group fitness classes, including yoga and spin, require advance booking through our mobile app at least two hours before the session begins.

A survey of 2,000 office workers found that those who slept seven to eight hours were twice as productive as colleagues who slept less. Some people believe that sleeping late at weekends can repair the damage of a short week, but researchers say this only helps partially. Experts recommend keeping regular bedtimes and avoiding screens for an hour before sleep.

reading.title: Shahar hayotining afzalliklari va qiyinchiliklari
reading.meta: True / False / Not Given · 4 ta savol

items.q: Good public transport allows city residents to travel conveniently without owning a private vehicle.
items.exp: Matnda "making it easy for residents to travel without owning a car" deb ta'kidlangan, shuning uchun bu tasdiq to'g'ri (True).

items.q: Buying a home in rural areas is generally more expensive than buying one in big cities.
items.exp: Matnda "housing costs in cities are often much higher compared to rural areas" deb yozilgan, ya'ni shaharda uy-joy qimmatroq. Shuning uchun bu tasdiq noto'g'ri (False).

items.q: City governments are currently spending more money to build modern public parks.
items.exp: Matnda parklar ko'ngilochar maskan sifatida tilga olingan bo'lsa-da, shahar hukumati yangi parklar qurishga pul ajratayotgani haqida hech qanday ma'lumot berilmagan (Not Given).

items.q: According to the passage, what is a primary cause of sleep problems for city dwellers?
items.exp: Matndagi "High noise levels from traffic and construction can cause stress and sleep problems" jumlasiga ko'ra, transport va qurilish shovqini uyqu muammolariga sabab bo'ladi. To'g'ri javob: B.

reading.text:
Living in a modern city offers many advantages, but it also comes with unique challenges. One of the greatest benefits of city life is convenience. Cities usually have excellent public transportation systems, such as buses, trams, and underground trains, making it easy for residents to travel without owning a car. In addition, urban areas provide a wide variety of job opportunities, educational institutions, and healthcare facilities. People can easily find diverse places for entertainment, including museums, parks, restaurants, and shopping centres, all within short distances.

However, life in a big city is not perfect. High noise levels from traffic and construction can cause stress and sleep problems for many residents. Furthermore, housing costs in cities are often much higher compared to rural areas, making it difficult for young professionals to buy their own homes. Pollution is another serious concern, as air quality in large cities often falls below recommended health standards. Despite these drawbacks, millions of people continue to move to urban centres every year because they prefer the vibrant lifestyle and endless opportunities that city environments provide. Overall, city living requires a balance between enjoying modern amenities and coping with daily urban pressures.
reading.en: The Advantages and Challenges of City Life

reading.title: Yapon choy marosimi san'ati
reading.meta: True / False / Not Given · 4 ta savol

items.q: The low entrance of the tearoom is designed to make guests feel equal regardless of their social standing.
items.exp: Matnda nijiriguchi deb ataluvchi past eshik barchani tiz cho'kib kirishga majbur qilib, ijtimoiy mavqeni ramziy ravishda yo'qotishi va tenglik o'rnatishi aytilgan ("symbolically stripping away social status and creating equality among participants").

items.q: Tea ceremonies are currently performed by most Japanese families on a daily basis.
items.exp: Matnga ko'ra, zamonaviy Yaponiyada urbanizatsiya va tezkor hayot sababli choy marosimlari kundalik hayotda kamdan-kam o'tkaziladi ("less common in daily life"), ya'ni ko'pchilik oilalar buni har kuni bajarmaydi.

items.q: Sen no Rikyū wrote several bestselling books explaining the philosophy of Chadō.
items.exp: Matnda usta Sen no Rikyū Chadō falsafasini rivojlantirgani qayd etilgan, biroq uning kitoblar yozganligi haqida hech qanday ma'lumot berilmagan.

items.q: According to the passage, what distinguishes the perspective of practitioners from that of outsiders regarding Chadō?
opts: Outsiders appreciate the strict etiquette more than practitioners do.
Practitioners view it as a form of meditation rather than just a social event.
Practitioners focus solely on the chemical benefits of matcha tea.
Outsiders regard the ceremony as an ancient religious requirement.
items.exp: Matnda tashqi kuzatuvchilar bu marosimni shunchaki ijtimoiy uchrashuv deb hisoblashsa-da, amaliyotchilar uni meditatsiya shakli deb bilishlari aniq ko'rsatilgan ("practitioners consider it a form of active meditation").

reading.text:
The Japanese tea ceremony, known as Chadō or "the Way of Tea," is a cultural ritual steeped in Zen Buddhist philosophy. Originating in the ninth century, when Buddhist monks first brought tea leaves from China, the practice evolved over centuries into a refined art form. By the sixteenth century, master Sen no Rikyū transformed Chadō by emphasizing the concepts of harmony, respect, purity, and tranquility.

Central to the ceremony is the preparation of matcha, a finely powdered green tea. The host prepares the beverage with meticulous movements, every gesture dictated by centuries of etiquette. Guests enter the tearoom through a deliberately low sliding door called a nijiriguchi, which forces everyone to crawl, symbolically stripping away social status and creating equality among participants. While outsiders often view the ritual as a mere social gathering, practitioners consider it a form of active meditation that encourages mindfulness and deep appreciation of the present moment.

In contemporary Japan, traditional tea ceremonies are less common in daily life due to modern urbanization and fast-paced schedules. Nevertheless, Chadō remains widely preserved through specialized schools and cultural clubs, continuing to influence Japanese aesthetic values, including hospitality and seasonal awareness.
reading.en: The Art of the Japanese Tea Ceremony

reading.title: Kvant biologiyasi va qushlarning navigatsiya siri
reading.meta: True / False / Not Given · 4 ta savol

items.q: Laboratory-based magnetic resonance experiments have supported the plausibility of the cryptochrome compass mechanism.
items.exp: Matnda "magnetic resonance studies have corroborated the feasibility of this biochemical compass in vitro" deb aytilgan, ya'ni laboratoriya (in vitro) sinovlari mexanizmning haqiqatga yaqinligini tasdiqlagan.

items.q: The intra-protein electron transfer in cryptochromes is initiated independently of external light stimulation.
items.exp: Matnga ko'ra, elektron almashinuvi yorug'liksiz emas, balki aynan ko'k yorug'lik ta'sirida qo'zg'alish ("Upon photoexcitation by blue light") orqali yuzaga keladi.

items.q: Migratory birds rely more heavily on geomagnetic sensitivity than on celestial cues during night migrations.
items.exp: Matnda geomagnit sezgirlik haqida so'z boradi, biroq qushlarning tunda osmon belgilariga (celestial cues) nisbatan magnit maydonga ko'proq tayanishi haqida hech qanday ma'lumot berilmagan.

items.q: According to the passage, why do critics question the cryptochrome hypothesis?
opts: Cryptochromes cannot be photoexcited under realistic environmental wavelengths.
Migratory birds consistently fail to detect ambient geomagnetic fields in wild conditions.
Avian retinas have been proven to lack the necessary tryptophan residues for electron transfer.
Quantum coherence would need to survive thermal disruption longer than standard kinetics predict.
items.exp: Matndagi "Skeptics point out that the radical pair's quantum coherence must persist against thermal decoherence far longer than conventional chemical kinetics suggest is plausible" jumlasi kvant kogerentligi termal shovqinga kutilganidan uzoqroq chidashi talab qilinishini tasdiqlaydi.

reading.text: Quantum biology explores non-trivial quantum phenomena in biological systems, once deemed impossible due to the warm, wet, and noisy cellular milieu. A seminal focus within this emerging discipline is avian magnetoreception, the sensory mechanism enabling migratory birds to navigate across planetary distances. The prevailing paradigm centers on cryptochromes—specialized flavoproteins located within avian retinas. Upon photoexcitation by blue light, a cryptochrome initiates an intra-protein electron transfer along a triad of tryptophan residues, generating a radical pair in a coherent quantum state. The spatiotemporal dynamics of this radical pair, specifically the interconversion between singlet and triplet spin states, are exquisitely sensitive to weak, ambient geomagnetic fields. Although magnetic resonance studies have corroborated the feasibility of this biochemical compass in vitro, translating these molecular behaviors to macro-scale navigational fidelity remains challenging. Skeptics point out that the radical pair's quantum coherence must persist against thermal decoherence far longer than conventional chemical kinetics suggest is plausible. Furthermore, the downstream neural pathways that transduce these quantum spin signals into perceivable visual or spatial cues in the avian brain have yet to be definitively mapped, leaving the empirical framework partially incomplete despite substantial biophysical modeling. Consequently, while quantum mechanics offers a compelling explanatory framework, absolute consensus eludes the scientific community.

reading.title: Shokolad tarixi va global ommabopligi
reading.meta: True / False / Not Given · 4 ta savol

items.q: The Maya and Aztec people consumed chocolate mainly as a liquid rather than a solid food.
items.exp: Tog'ri. Matnda "They did not eat chocolate in solid bars as we do now; instead, they drank it as a bitter beverage" deb ta'kidlangan.

items.q: Spanish explorers were the first to add chili peppers to cacao drinks.
items.exp: Noto'g'ri. Matnga ko'ra, qalampirni qadimgi Maya va Atsteklar qo'shishgan, ispanlar esa shakar va sut qo'shishgan.

items.q: The majority of cacao bean farmers in West Africa live below the poverty line.
items.exp: Berilmagan. Matnda G'arbiy Afrikadagi kakao ishlab chiqarish miqdori aytilgan, ammo fermerlarning daromadi yoki kambag'allik darajasi haqida ma'lumot yo'q.

items.q: Which country is currently the world's biggest exporter of cacao beans?
items.exp: Matndagi "...with Ivory Coast being the largest individual exporter" jumlasiga ko'ra javob Kot-d'Ivuar hisoblanadi.

reading.text:
Chocolate is one of the most popular foods in the world today, enjoyed by millions of people every day. However, its history began thousands of years ago in Central and South America. The ancient Maya and Aztec civilizations were the first to cultivate cacao trees. They did not eat chocolate in solid bars as we do now; instead, they drank it as a bitter beverage mixed with spices and chili peppers. They believed cacao seeds were a gift from the gods and even used them as a form of money.

In the sixteenth century, Spanish explorers brought cacao back to Europe. European cooks added sugar and milk to suit local tastes, transforming the bitter drink into a sweet luxury for royalty. It was not until the nineteenth century that modern machinery allowed companies to manufacture solid eating chocolate on a large scale.

Today, chocolate production is a massive global industry. West Africa produces more than sixty percent of the world's cacao beans, with Ivory Coast being the largest individual exporter. Although chocolate contains antioxidants that may offer health benefits, experts warn that consuming too much sweet chocolate can lead to health problems like tooth decay and weight gain due to high sugar levels.
reading.en: The History and Global Appeal of Chocolate

reading.title: Zamonaviy Olimpiya O'yinlari va Texnologiya
reading.meta: True / False / Not Given · 4 ta savol

items.q: Women were not allowed to compete in the 1896 Athens Olympic Games.
items.exp: Matndagi 'Initially, the Games featured a limited number of events and only male participants' jumlasiga ko'ra, 1896-yilgi birinchi o'yinlarda faqat erkaklar qatnashgan.

items.q: Modern synthetic running surfaces have resulted in slower race times compared to older cinder tracks.
items.exp: Matnda zamonaviy sintetik yo'lakchalar poyga vaqtini sekinlashtirmagan, aksincha tezroq natijalarga ('contributing to faster race times') olib kelgani ta'kidlangan.

items.q: The majority of Olympic athletes prefer traditional equipment over high-tech gear.
items.exp: Matnda texnologiyalardan foydalanish haqida aytilgan bo'lsa-da, ko'pchilik sportchilar an'anaviy jihozlarni afzal ko'rish-ko'rmasligi haqida ma'lumot berilmagan.

items.q: What is one major concern raised by critics regarding the use of advanced technology in sports?
opts: It provides an unfair benefit to richer countries.
It leads to a higher frequency of physical injuries.
It reduces spectator enjoyment during live matches.
It completely replaces the need for human coaches.
items.exp: Matndagi 'some critics argue that technology creates an unfair advantage for wealthier nations' jumlasiga ko'ra, tanqidchilar texnologiya boy davlatlarga adolatsiz ustunlik beradi deb xavotir bildiradilar.

reading.text:
The modern Olympic Games have undergone significant transformations since their revival in Athens in 1896. Initially, the Games featured a limited number of events and only male participants. Over the decades, the event expanded to include women, winter sports, and a vastly larger array of athletic disciplines. However, the most profound changes in recent years have been driven by technological advancements.

Today, advanced technology plays a critical role in both athlete training and officiating. High-speed cameras, wearable sensors, and motion analysis software allow coaches to monitor an athlete's biomechanics in real time. This data helps reduce injury risks and optimize performance. In sports like track and field, modern synthetic running surfaces have replaced traditional cinder tracks, contributing to faster race times and new world records.

Furthermore, video assistant referee (VAR) systems and electronic scoring have minimized human errors in officiating. Despite these benefits, some critics argue that technology creates an unfair advantage for wealthier nations that can afford expensive equipment. Consequently, governing bodies are working to establish regulations that balance technological innovation with the traditional principles of sportsmanship and equal opportunity.

grammar.title: O'zlashtirma nutq (Reported Speech) bo'yicha grammatik testlar

items.q: She promised that she ___ the report by the following day.
items.exp: O'zlashtirma gapda asosiy fe'l o'tgan zamonda bo'lsa, kelasi zamon ko'rsatkichi 'will' bir pog'ona orqaga surilib 'would' shakliga o me'yoran o'zgaradi.

items.q: The professor suggested ___ the research data before drawing any final conclusions.
items.exp: 'Suggest' fe'lidan so'ng bevosita to'ldiruvchi kelmaganda, undan keyingi fe me'yoran ing-forma (-ing) shaklida ishlatiladi.

items.q: The investigator asked the witness where ___ at the time of the incident.
items.exp: O'zlashtirma so'roq gaplarda so'z tartibi darak gapnikidek (ega + kesim) bo'ladi va zamon Past Perfect (he had been) shakliga o'tadi.

items.q: The manager reminded us that we ___ submit the quarterly reports by Friday afternoon.
items.exp: O'zlashtirma gapda majburiyatni bildiruvchi 'must' yoki 'have to' modal fe'llari o'tgan zamonda 'had to' shakliga o'zgaradi.

items.q: She admitted that if she ___ harder in her youth, she would have achieved her goals much earlier.
items.exp: Uchinchi tur shartli gaplar (3rd conditional) o'zlashtirma gapga aylantirilganda zamon shakli (Past Perfect - had studied) o'zgarmasdan qoladi.

grammar.title: Sifat va ravishlarning qiyosiy hamda orttirma darajalari (Advanced Comparatives & Superlatives)

items.q: The ___ the research methodology employed in the study, the more reliable the final survey results will be.
items.exp: 'The + qiyosiy daraja..., the + qiyosiy daraja...' (qanchalik..., shunchalik...) parallel o'zgarish strukturasida birinchi qismda ham qiyosiy daraja ('more rigorous') ishlatilishi shart.

items.q: Electric vehicles are now considered by many industry analysts to be ___ superior to traditional petrol cars in terms of long-term efficiency.
items.exp: 'Superior' sifati o'zida qiyosiy ma'noni bergani uchun uning oldidan 'more' ishlatilmaydi. Qiyosiy ma'noni kuchaytirish uchun 'vastly' (sezilarli darajada) ravishi qo'llaniladi.

items.q: The latest quantum computer is reported to process complex algorithms nearly five times ___ than its predecessor.
items.exp: Gap oxirida 'than' bog'lovchisi bo'lgani uchun karra ko'payishini ko'rsatuvchi 'five times' iborasidan so'ng qiyosiy daraja ('faster') keladi.

items.q: Of all the renewable energy sources currently available, offshore wind power has shown ___ potential for large-scale urban development.
items.exp: Barcha manbalar orasida eng yuqori darajani va ustunlikni ta'kidlash uchun 'by far' kuchaytiruvchi iborasi orttirma darajadagi sifat ('the greatest') bilan birga ishlatiladi.

items.q: The economic repercussions of the policy turned out to be ___ severe than initially projected by financial experts.
items.exp: Qiyosiy darajadagi 'more severe' iborasini kuchaytirish uchun 'substantially' (anchagina, sezilarli darajada) ravishi qo'llaniladi. 'Very' qiyosiy daraja bilan dog'ul ishlatilmaydi.

items.q: Many students enjoy ___ in group discussions during IELTS preparation classes.
items.exp: 'Enjoy' fe'lidan keyin har doim fe'lning gerund (-ing) shakli ishlatiladi. Shuning uchun 'participating' to'g'ri javobdir.

items.q: After careful consideration, she decided ___ for the IELTS exam in December.
items.exp: 'Decide' fe'lidan keyin fe'lning 'to' bilan keladigan infinitiv shakli ishlatiladi. Shuning uchun 'to register' to'g'ri javob.

items.q: Candidates should avoid ___ repetitive vocabulary in the IELTS Speaking test.
items.exp: 'Avoid' fe'li o'zidan keyin har doim gerund (-ing) shaklini talab qiladi. Shuning uchun 'using' to'g'ri keladi.

items.q: He hopes ___ a overall band score of 7.5 in his next attempt.
items.exp: 'Hope' fe'lidan keyin har doim 'to' bilan keladigan infinitiv shakli ishlatiladi. Shu sababli 'to achieve' to'g'ri javob.

items.q: The tutor suggested ___ more listening practice to improve overall comprehension.
items.exp: 'Suggest' fe'lidan so'ng bevosita fe'l kelsa, u gerund (-ing) shaklida bo'lishi kerak. Shuning uchun 'doing' to'g'ri javob.

writing: Some people believe that governments should spend money on public transport rather than building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many people now work from home. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this trend.
In many countries, young people spend too much time on social media. What problems does this cause and what can be done?
Some people think university education should be free for everyone. Others think students should pay. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Nowadays more people choose to live alone. Is this a positive or negative development?

In many modern cities, the sense of community among residents is declining as urban populations continue to grow. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures can be taken to address it?

As cities expand, some people argue that local governments should prioritize creating public parks and green spaces over building new housing. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

In many countries, traditional festivals and customs are disappearing as a result of globalization. Some people believe that governments should invest significant public funds to keep these traditions alive, while others argue that this money would be better spent on modern public services. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

In many parts of the world, younger generations are showing less interest in their local culture and heritage than previous generations did. What are the causes of this trend, and what measures can be taken to encourage young people to value their cultural roots?

Some people believe that the increasing influence of global media is causing traditional local cultures to fade away, and that governments should take strict measures to protect local traditions. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

In many parts of the world, historical sites and cultural monuments are being damaged by mass tourism. What problems does this cause, and what measures can be taken to protect these cultural heritage sites?

Governments should allocate public funding primarily to scientific research that solves immediate environmental problems, rather than spending money on space exploration. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
In recent years, fewer young people are choosing to study science subjects in higher education. What are the main causes of this trend, and what solutions can be implemented to address it?

In many countries, fast food is becoming cheaper and more accessible than traditional, healthy meals. Some people believe that governments should impose higher taxes on unhealthy food products to discourage people from buying them. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

A significant amount of food produced globally is lost or wasted every year before it reaches consumers. What are the main causes of this food waste, and what solutions can governments and individuals implement to address this issue?
speaking:
Describe a teacher who influenced you.
You should say: who this person was, what they taught you, how they behaved in class, and explain why they influenced you.

Describe a place in your city that you like to visit.
You should say: where it is, how often you go there, what you do there, and explain why you like it.

Describe a time when you helped someone.
You should say: who you helped, how you helped them, why they needed help, and how you felt afterwards.

Describe a useful app on your phone.
You should say: what it is, how often you use it, what it does, and explain why it is useful.

Describe a family celebration you remember well.
You should say: what the occasion was, who was there, what you did, and explain why you remember it.
